_intro: Hydro p1 runs at rot 298-300 (5 dumps) post-processed with a 3-D GPU ray tracer (tools/em3d.py): rays through the cubed-sphere grid at 40 orbital phases, petitRADTRANS 3.4 R=1000 correlated-k (H2O, CO, CO2, CH4, OH, HCN, TiO, VO, FeH, Na, K, SiO) premixed by random overlap and rebinned to R~200, FastChem 3 equilibrium chemistry with local condensation (1x solar Asplund 2009 = the run EOS), H- bound-free/free-free, H2-H2/H2-He CIA, no clouds, no scattering, no reflected light; PHOENIX stars (Delrez 2016 / Ehrenreich 2020 parameters). Fe I: the fe_hires tool, per exposure. Model band = spread over the 5 dumps.

obs_summary.png.take: Not consistent: the model hotspot is ~29 deg east (observed 0-6 deg), the nightside is 3x too bright at 3-5 um and the dayside 19-13 % too faint, in both planets.
obs_summary.png.alt: model vs observed day flux, night flux, offset, brightness temperature per band
obs_summary.png.cap: Diamonds: model (Fourier fit of the phase curve; day = phase 0.5, night = phase 0). Dots: observed, 1 sigma. Brightness temperatures use the observed Rp/Rs and the same PHOENIX star.

obs_w121_phasecurves.png.take: WASP-121b: amplitude too small and peak too early in every band; NIRSpec NRS2 day 3989 vs 4924 ppm, night 1804 vs 630 ppm, peak offset +33 vs +2.7 deg.
obs_w121_phasecurves.png.alt: WASP-121b phase curves model vs JWST, Spitzer, HST
obs_w121_phasecurves.png.cap: Blue: model with the dump-to-dump spread. NIRSpec points: Evans-Soma 2025 band means (Zenodo). Spitzer: Morello 2023 and Davenport 2025. WFC3: Mikal-Evans 2022 binned. SOSS: Splinter 2025.

obs_w121_spectra.png.take: WASP-121b: the dayside spectrum has the right shape (1.4 um water and 4.5 um CO in emission, i.e. an inversion) but sits ~15-25 %% low; the nightside is 2-5x too bright.
obs_w121_spectra.png.alt: WASP-121b dayside and nightside emission spectra
obs_w121_spectra.png.cap: Data binned for display. Dayside: Kahle 2026 (NIRISS, NIRSpec at eclipse), Mikal-Evans 2020 (WFC3), Morello 2023 (Spitzer). Nightside: Evans-Soma 2025 phase 0.925-0.95, Mikal-Evans 2022, Morello 2023.

obs_w76_phasecurves.png.take: WASP-76b: Spitzer 4.5 um eclipse 2914 vs 3729 ppm, night 1379 vs ~800 ppm, peak offset +32 vs +0.7 deg; same pattern as WASP-121b.
obs_w76_phasecurves.png.alt: WASP-76b Spitzer phase curves and dayside spectrum
obs_w76_phasecurves.png.cap: May & Stevenson 2021 eclipse depth and derived nightside; Dang 2025; HST WFC3 Fu 2021 and Edwards 2020 (different dilution corrections). No JWST phase curve of WASP-76b is published.

obs_fe_timeresolved.png.take: Fe I through transit: WASP-76b matches Ehrenreich 2020 (model -4.5 / -10.1 km/s first / second half vs -3.9 / -10.8, rms 1.7 km/s); WASP-121b is too blueshifted late in transit (-10.4 vs -7.2 km/s).
obs_fe_timeresolved.png.alt: Fe I line centre and depth vs orbital phase, model vs ESPRESSO
obs_fe_timeresolved.png.cap: Model: fe_hires per-exposure CCF with the pRT 3000 K Fe I template, planet rest frame, Gaussian fit; solid = both limbs as observed, dashed = one limb. Depths: CCF amplitude (template-weighted) vs observed CCF depth/contrast, so absolute depths are only roughly comparable. Data digitised where marked.

obs_clouds_w121.png.take: WASP-121b (G395H_NRS2): clouds can bring the nightside to 1173 ppm (observed 630, clear 1804) and the offset to +31 deg (observed +2.7, clear +33); best overall case B_3H_r1: night 1173, amplitude 3256 vs 4294, offset +31 deg, but the dayside stays at 3984 vs 4924 ppm (clouds do not form there).
obs_clouds_w121.png.alt: WASP-121b cloud grid: night flux, amplitude, offset, day flux vs particle radius
obs_clouds_w121.png.cap: Post-processing only: condensate clouds placed in the frozen hydro T(p) (no radiative feedback, so the cloud does not heat the layers below or change the winds). Recipe (Parmentier+16/21, Roman & Rauscher 17/19, Roman+21, Frazier+26; notes in obscheck_1102/lit/clouds_notes.md): species condense where T < T_cond(p) (Visscher+10, Wakeford+17, 1x solar), cloud from the column base up 1 H, 3 H (0.43, 1.3 dex) or to the model top; species sets A = Al2O3+CaTiO3, C = A + Mg2SiO4+MgSiO3, B = C + Fe; full condensable mass (one f = 0.1 case); monodisperse radius 0.1/1/5 um, pRT Mie opacities; filled = extinction with (1-g)-scaled scattering counted as absorption, open = absorption only (no scattering in the tracer). Points: mean and spread over the 5 dumps, 20 phases each.

obs_clouds_w76.png.take: WASP-76b (IRAC2): clouds can bring the nightside to 991 ppm (observed 801, clear 1379) and the offset to +31 deg (observed +0.7, clear +32); best overall case C_3H_r1: night 1010, amplitude 2184 vs 2928, offset +32 deg, but the dayside stays at 2909 vs 3729 ppm (clouds do not form there).

obs_clouds_summary.png.take: Best cloud deck per planet: WASP-121b: night not fixed (1173 vs 630 ppm), amplitude not fixed (3256 vs 4294 ppm), offset not fixed (+31 vs +2.7 deg); dayside 19 % low; WASP-76b: night fixed, amplitude not fixed (2184 vs 2928 ppm), offset not fixed (+32 vs +0.7 deg); dayside 22 % low. Clouds do not form on the hot dayside, so they cannot remove the dayside deficit.
obs_clouds_summary.png.alt: best cloud-deck phase curve vs clear model vs data
